foundItems.title: The Hyphen Unites: Avi Shlaim on Arab-Jewish Life
foundItems.description: Avi Shlaim, historian and influential scholar of Israel’s relationship with the Arab world, joins John Plotz and Yuval Evri to discuss class, caste differences, and destructive ethno-nationalist ideologies in mainstream Israeli politics. The post The Hyphen Unites: Avi Shlaim on Arab-Jewish Life appeared first on Public Books.

foundItems.title: The Life of the Mind of a Factory Worker
foundItems.description: “Beware to those who read ‘Adrift in the South’ solely as a cautionary tale about the Chinese state without considering the international flows of goods and power.” The post The Life of the Mind of a Factory Worker appeared first on Public Books.

foundItems.title: Long-Distance Talkers: The Great Depression Speaks
foundItems.description: During the Great Depression, the Works Progress Administration conducted thousands of interviews among American workers. Anne Trubek's “American Made” gives them new voice. The post Long-Distance Talkers: The Great Depression Speaks appeared first on Public Books.

foundItems.title: If We Rot, You Rot with Us
foundItems.description: “Despite the enduring belief that literary nonsense is primarily directed toward children—an idea that has its roots in the popularity of Lewis Carroll and Dr. Seuss—literary nonsense has historically been weaponized by the masses, always under the guise of stupidity, to effect change.” The post If We Rot, You Rot with Us appeared first on Public Books.

foundItems.title: The Last Graduate Students?
foundItems.description: “I began writing this as a record of what it felt like to be a student then, as collective attachments to values—long recognized as fraying, with the knell of the next scapegoat, or horrifying spectacle—face the final chopping block: public good, responsibility to others, democracy itself.” The post The Last Graduate Students? appeared first on Public Books.

foundItems.title: The Treachery of Machine Realism
foundItems.description: “The bombed elementary school in Iran appears to have become a target thanks to satellite imaging. In this case, what the image represented — and to who — was a matter of life and death.” The post The Treachery of Machine Realism appeared first on Public Books.

foundItems.title: The Uninhabitable Front
foundItems.description: “Israeli military aircraft flew low over the Lebanese villages of Ras Naqoura and Aita al-Shaab, spraying agricultural fields with a fine mist... Within days, the green of fields, orchards, and olive groves turned brown. Farmers who had worked the same soil for generations watched their trees die.” The post The Uninhabitable Front appeared first on Public Books.

foundItems.title: “Being Undocumented Is Already a Chronic Stress. Then, Add in Blackness”: Talking with Dr. Felecia Russell on the Experience of Black Undocumented Folks
foundItems.description: "Growing up, I really didn't get exposed to the conversations about immigration, until I found out that I didn't have the proper documentation. Once I learned that, my world, I felt, just really shattered." The post “Being Undocumented Is Already a Chronic Stress. Then, Add in Blackness”: Talking with Dr. Felecia Russell on the Experience of Black Undocumented Folks appeared first on Public Books.

foundItems.title: Remember Them: Palestine Scholars Murdered in the Gaza Genocide
foundItems.description: “In Palestine, some 87,000 students have suffered a near total disruption of their studies for the duration of the genocide, and more than 1200 have been killed. Upwards of 200 academic staff have perished, many in targeted attacks.” The post Remember Them: Palestine Scholars Murdered in the Gaza Genocide appeared first on Public Books.
